cvEn:
Efraim Sharabi, son of Hana and Isashar, was born in 1936 in the Hatikva neighborhood of Tel Aviv. He attended a primary school. His childhood was spent in the poverty-stricken neighborhood, and especially after he was orphaned of his mother, he endured great suffering until he was forced to leave his home. His wanderings then began, from one institution to another, and eventually he arrived at Ashdot Ya'akov. Life's hardships taught him a bitter lesson, so that he was reticent and distrustful of everyone. But within the youth society at Ashdot Ya'akov, it seems, his wounded spirit was healed, as revealed by the faint smile on his lips and the cheerful songs he sang from time to time. He became a member of the kibbutz, and then his time came to join the ranks of the fighters.

In August 1954 he was drafted into the IDF, and he fell in battle at the Mitla Pass in the Sinai Campaign on 26 Marheshvan 5717 (31 October 1956). He was brought to burial at the Military Cemetery for Emergencies in Shelah, and on 12 Marheshvan 5718 (6 November 1957) he was reinterred in the Military Cemetery in Kiryat Shaul. His memory was commemorated in the Tevet 5717 issue of *Dapim* (publication of the Department for Children and Youth Aliyah of the Jewish Agency, Jerusalem). He was also mentioned in *Niv HaKvutza* of the Shevet 5717 issue. His memory was further recorded in Uri Milstein's book *Milhamot HaTzanhanim* (The Paratroopers' Wars).
